text:
Predicates:
AtSchool(x) ::: x is at Mary's school.
WorksInStudentJobs(x) ::: x works in student jobs on campus.
OrderTakeoutFrequently(x) ::: x orders takeout frequently in college.
EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ::: x enjoys the dining hall meals and recipes.
PickyEater(x) ::: x is a picky eater.
SpendTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x) ::: x spends a lot of time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
NeedsMoney(x) ::: x needs to earn money to help pay for college tuition.
Question: (The question is a statement to be evaluated.)
Premises:
AtSchool(Hannah) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school.
WorksInStudentJobs(Hannah) ∧ (NeedsMoney(Hannah) → (¬PickyEater(Hannah) ∧ NeedsMoney(Hannah))) ::: Hannah works in student jobs, and if she needs to earn money, then she is neither a picky eater nor needs to earn money.
OrderTakeoutFrequently(Hannah) → WorksInStudentJobs(Hannah) ::: If Hannah orders takeout frequently, then she works in student jobs.
OrderTakeoutFrequently(Hannah) ∨ (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(Hannah) ∧ ¬PickyEater(Hannah)) ::: Hannah either orders takeout frequently or enjoys the dining hall meals and is not a picky eater.
EnjoysDiningHallMeals(Hannah) → ¬PickyEater(Hannah) ::: If Hannah enjoys the dining hall meals, then she is not a picky eater.
EnjoysDiningHallMeals(Hannah) → SpendTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(Hannah) ::: If Hannah enjoys the dining hall meals, then she spends a lot of her time eating and catching up with friends.
Conclusion:
Hannah ∧ ¬PickyEater(Hannah) ∧ SpendTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(Hannah) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school, not a picky eater, and spends a lot of her time eating and catching up.
